name: Fixed15: historical RankIC versus LightGBM versus CatBoost
features: Original 13 traditional factors; fixed feature list, no news, announcements, added candidate factors, industry feature or stock identifier
label: Raw adjusted-close return from signal+1 close to signal+6 close, measured on the full exchange session calendar; no quote filling
training_frequency: Weekly point-in-time factor cross-sections within the trailing 252 market sessions, inclusive of the signal session; only labels ending strictly before refit are used
refit: First evaluation weekly signal of each calendar month; models held fixed until next refit
training_universe: Same broad valid-original-fixed-score candidates at each historical signal, pooled by row without per-date weighting; both areas share one trained model
missing_features: Training sample medians only, all-missing training column falls back to zero; prediction membership never depends on future label availability
backend: Reuse factors.factor_ml model constructors, but require exact backend, no silent fallback; 80 trees, learning rate 0.05, depth4, seed42, CPU threads2, no tuning or early stopping
lightgbm: num_leaves15, subsample0.8 with inherited subsample_freq0 (therefore no row bagging), colsample_bytree0.8; deterministic and force_col_wise enabled
selection: Unchanged weekly fixed15, top100, buffer top30, industry maximum3, correlation cap0.8, daily volatility budget; TECH15 filters five historical industries before top100 and allows all15 in tech
baseline: Reuse sealed asset-repaired BASE_WEEKLY and BASE_TECH15_WEEKLY accounts at matching fees; preserve their daily-label RankIC estimation
failure_policy: Missing backend, insufficient initial training history, nonfinite predictions, unhandled corporate action or changed frozen inputs abort; never replace model or zero asset
interpretation: Comparison of three complete scoring recipes, not a pure model-only causal ablation: ML uses weekly training rows while baseline RankIC uses daily IC observations; raw-return loss differs from rank-correlation weighting
limitations: Dates and strategy were already studied: chronological walk-forward is not a previously untouched holdout.
Missing future prices exclude training labels, not prediction candidates; suspension/delisting label availability can bias the learning sample.
Inherit point-in-time data vendor revisions, financial proxy and industry coverage limitations.
Fractional shares, no lot sizes, minimum commission, tax schedule, price-limit queue or capacity checks.
No automatic promotion into paper/live accounts and no claim that either model solves excess-return weakness.
